correctness.rationale: For every n>=2, the code is a sensor subset in the open path prism with unique nonempty closed-neighborhood signatures. A graph-distance locality lemma requires comparison only at rung difference <=2. The five-mask predicate therefore yields an exact 256-state, 737-transition integer min-plus recurrence with fixed right-end testing. Exhaustive calculation of all components proves v_6(a,b,c,d)=3+[a=3]+wt(b)+wt(c)+wt(d) and v_13=v_6+6; since the min-plus map commutes with translation, v_{n+7}=v_n+6 for all n>=6 by induction. All seven base values plus n=2..5 have finite exact independent checks, and explicit optimum sensor sets are directly verified through width 13. The formula and equality to prior circular values follow without heuristic extrapolation or tolerance.

originality.rationale: The all-length numerical expression matches the *known circular* height-two optimum of Bouznif et al. (2019), which is explicitly credited; the claim instead establishes the same exact expression for finite non-circular ladders and proves equality despite changed end edges. The 2004 paper gives only the infinite two-row density and a general grid algorithm; the 2016 prism paper gives bounds. The 2019 paper supplies a general non-circular shortest-path procedure but no explicit open-width-two closed form or boundary equality. The new 256-component min-plus identity proves the missing finite evaluation for all lengths. Publicly indexed nearby results for total identifying domination of *circular* prisms concern a different graph and stronger total-domination condition. Priority is qualified by possible unindexed earlier finite computations.

value.rationale: The precise effect of closing two endpoint rungs on the minimum number of identifying sensors is a motivated graph-network design question. The result shows exact finite-size boundary neutrality for all widths at least five despite altered signatures. The known infinite 3/7 density does not determine all residue classes, and a generic transfer algorithm does not exhibit the simple equality. A compact exact all-n certificate makes the boundary theorem reusable and checkable, without claiming a larger grid result or full optimizer classification.
